Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 7
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a critical error in interpreting the definition of "sunrise" and its frequency. In Step 7, the Planner incorrectly concluded that "Sunrise: approximately 1 time per year per location (polar reference)" and used this to claim the Full Moon is the most frequent event. This contradicts the fundamental astronomical fact that sunrise occurs daily (once per day) for the vast majority of the Earth's surface, not just once a year. The Planner confused the frequency of sunrise at the poles (where there is one continuous day and one continuous night per year) with the global or typical frequency. By adopting this incorrect "polar reference" as the standard for comparison, the Planner reversed the correct answer (Sunrise) to an incorrect one (Full Moon). This error stems from a failure to correctly synthesize the information gathered in Step 1 (which confirmed sunrise occurs daily) and applying a flawed, location-specific constraint to the entire problem without justification.
